ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square grid, and the shaded quadrilateral is labeled in order as P, Q, R, S. Taking the upper-left grid intersection as (0,0), with the positive x direction to the right and the positive y direction downward, by counting squares in the figure the vertices can be read as P=(1,1), Q=(2,5), R=(5,6), S=(8,2), with the unit being the side length of a small grid square. Reasoning: Use the shoelace formula to calculate the area of the quadrilateral. The forward product sum is 1×5 + 2×6 + 5×2 + 8×1 = 5 + 12 + 10 + 8 = 35. The backward product sum is 1×2 + 5×5 + 6×8 + 2×1 = 2 + 25 + 48 + 2 = 77. Area = |35 - 77| / 2 = 21 grid square units. The side length of each small square is 2 cm, so the area of each grid square unit is 2×2=4 cm². Therefore the area of the quadrilateral is 21×4=84 cm².

method.method_draft: Use grid coordinates and the shoelace formula. From the image, take the top-left grid intersection as (0,0) and count cells right/down to read the quadrilateral vertices as P=(1,1), Q=(2,5), R=(5,6), and S=(8,2) in grid-cell units. From the text, note that each grid cell is 2 cm by 2 cm, so one grid-square unit has area 4 cm^2. Apply the shoelace formula to P,Q,R,S to get the polygon area in cell units, then multiply by 4 to convert to square centimeters, giving 84 cm^2.
